stakes: The Mammoth go in tied for sixth in the Central with 31 points, a point behind the Stars, tied for third. A regulation win for the Mammoth would lift them past the Stars. The Stars have two games in hand.

DAL.head: Too close to call
DAL.body: Utah has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately, but Dallas has home-ice advantage, and the Mammoth will be without Schmidt. For the Stars, the difference could be a power play that gets going.

UTA.head: Nothing to separate these two
UTA.body: Utah has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately, but Dallas has home-ice advantage, and the Mammoth will be without Schmidt. For the Mammoth, the difference could be keeping shots to a minimum.

story.head: Johnston’s favorite opponent
paras: The Stars (15-8-2) lost 5-3 to St. Louis last night, while the Mammoth have won two in a row. This is a Central Division matchup, with the Mammoth seventh (tied for 14th in the NHL) and the Stars fourth (tied for ninth). The Central has been the strongest of the four divisions so far.

The Mammoth have played better than their record (.574) says: their chances are worth about .705, and their goaltending has held them back. The Stars’ record (.640) is about what their chances are worth.

The Mammoth rarely get pinned in their own end (1st) and let the point shots come and guard the net (1st), but have had shaky goaltending (31st). On the other side, the Stars block more shots than anyone (1st), play slow, tight games (lowest) and kill penalties well (1st). Dallas has allowed 2.48 goals a game, the third fewest in the league. Something has to give when the Mammoth’s shooting runs into the Stars’ defense, and the Mammoth have the edge over the Stars on depth.

Clayton Keller (6 G / 25 A / 31 P in 26 GP) leads the Mammoth in scoring. Logan Cooley (13 G / 16 A / 29 P in 24 GP) has a team-high 13 goals, with seven points in his last five games. Jason Robertson (12 G / 17 A / 29 P in 25 GP) is tied for the Stars’ scoring lead, with seven points in his last five games. Mikko Rantanen (10 G / 19 A / 29 P in 25 GP) shares it, with seven points in his last five games and a point in seven straight games against Utah.
Sebastian Cossa (6-3-1 / .881 SV% in 10 GS) is in line to start for Utah. Jake Oettinger (13-5-1 / .912 SV% in 19 GS) has been terrific for Dallas and will likely start.

items.text: Wyatt Johnston has a point in seven straight games against Utah.

The Mammoth are newly without Michael Carcone, and have been without Nate Schmidt, John Marino and Nick Schmaltz for several games. Taking into account how much value each of these missing players usually adds, no team is missing more right now.
The Stars have been without Lian Bichsel since Nov 12.
Roope Hintz is one goal from 200.
